vcredist.name: Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable
vcredist.description: Runtime libraries required by programs built with Visual C++. Most common cause of missing DLL errors on Windows.

140.note: Covers Visual Studio 2015, 2017, 2019, and 2022 — all use the same runtime

fix_steps: Download the correct Visual C++ Redistributable from Microsoft
Run the installer — it will say 'Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable'
Click 'Install' and wait for it to finish
Restart your computer
Try opening the program again
vcredist.install_both_note: If you are not sure whether your program is 32-bit or 64-bit, install BOTH the x86 (32-bit) and x64 (64-bit) versions. This is safe and common.

ucrt.name: Universal C Runtime (Windows Update)
ucrt.description: Core Windows component. Usually fixed by running Windows Update rather than downloading separately.
fix_steps: Open Settings (press the Windows key, then click the gear icon)
Click 'Update & Security' (or 'Windows Update' on Windows 11)
Click 'Check for updates'
Install all available updates
Restart your computer
If the error persists, also install the Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable
ucrt.note: These DLLs are part of the Universal CRT which ships with Windows 10+. On older Windows (7/8), they come via Windows Update KB2999226.

dotnet.name: .NET Runtime
dotnet.description: Required by programs built with Microsoft .NET technology.
fix_steps: The program needs the .NET Runtime installed
Go to Microsoft's .NET download page
Download the '.NET Desktop Runtime' (not the SDK — you only need the runtime)
Run the installer and follow the steps
Restart your computer, then try opening the program again
dotnet.note: The error message usually says which version of .NET is needed (e.g., '.NET 6.0 Runtime'). If not specified, try the latest .NET 8 Desktop Runtime.

directx.name: DirectX Runtime
directx.description: Graphics and multimedia libraries used by games and media software.
fix_steps: Download the DirectX End-User Runtime Web Installer from Microsoft
Run the installer — it is called 'dxwebsetup.exe'
Follow the steps to install (uncheck any optional offers)
Restart your computer
Try opening the game or program again
directx.note: Many games include DirectX in their installer. If you just installed the game, try running the game's setup again and look for a 'DirectX' or 'Prerequisites' option.

openal.name: OpenAL (Audio Library)
openal.description: Audio library used by some games.
fix_steps: Download OpenAL from openal.org
Run the installer
Restart and try the game again

physx.name: NVIDIA PhysX
physx.description: Physics engine used by some games.
fix_steps: Download PhysX from NVIDIA's website
Run the installer
Restart and try the game again

vb_runtime.name: Visual Basic Runtime
vb_runtime.description: Required by older programs built with Visual Basic.
vb_runtime.note: These DLLs are included with Windows. If missing, run 'sfc /scannow' from an admin Command Prompt to repair system files.

windows_system.name: Windows System File
windows_system.description: Core Windows files that should never be missing. Usually indicates system corruption.
fix_steps: Open the Start Menu and search for 'Command Prompt'
Right-click on Command Prompt and choose 'Run as administrator'
Type: sfc /scannow (then press Enter)
Wait for it to finish — it may take 10-15 minutes
If it says it found and fixed problems, restart your computer
If problems remain, try: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
windows_system.note: Missing Windows system DLLs are serious. They should never need to be downloaded separately — if they are missing, Windows itself is damaged and needs repair.

safety_rules: NEVER suggest downloading individual DLL files from third-party websites
NEVER recommend sites like dll-files.com, dll-download.com, or any 'DLL download' site — they often bundle malware
ALWAYS recommend the official Microsoft installer or the program's own installer
If the DLL belongs to a specific program (not Windows/runtime), the fix is to reinstall that program
If a system DLL is missing, use sfc /scannow — do NOT download it from the internet
When in doubt, reinstalling the program that shows the error is always a safe first step
common_error_patterns: The program can't start because {dll} is missing from your computer
The code execution cannot proceed because {dll} was not found
This application failed to start because {dll} was not found
The procedure entry point could not be located in {dll}
System error: {dll} is not designed to run on Windows

diagnostic_commands.check_installed_redists: wmic product where "name like '%Visual C++%'" get name,version
